turns.assessment: The outage is a shared optical failure, not a svc230 client-port fault: many unrelated services failed simultaneously and numerous lightpaths reported OCH_LOS. Every affected working path depends on E1, and the simultaneous AMP_INPUT_LOS on two different outgoing OMSs from S06 indicates that channels were blocked before they diverged, consistent with failure of a common ROADM WSS input port at S06. An OTN-switch failure would not explain the optical LOS alarms, while a single OMS patch or span fault would not suppress both outgoing directions.

proposals.rationale: A failed WSS input port at roadm.S06 blocks every channel arriving on the common degree. This explains the common dependency of all affected working paths, the network-wide service impact, and loss of input on multiple outgoing S06 OMSs after the blocked channels would have diverged.

clarify.assessment: The evidence localizes the fault to a WSS input port at roadm.S06, but it does not identify which incoming degree failed. The two AMP_INPUT_LOS alarms are on different outgoing OMSs and are compatible with any common input port feeding them; the unchanged incoming channel monitors do not discriminate because a WSS port failure occurs after those measurements. Choosing among the S21, S11, S19, and S23 input ports would therefore be speculative.

llm_alone.decision: commit not to one place (4 locations); reported as a set
